name: 2D vehicle kinematics (kinematic bicycle model: accelerate, brake, steer)
description: Steps a top-down car with the kinematic bicycle model used in PythonRobotics: position from speed and heading, heading from speed, wheelbase and clipped steering angle, speed from acceleration. Answers "how far and where does the car go with this throttle/steer sequence?" and fixes the car parameters the game uses.
author: Skillpack contributors

copyright_lines_verbatim: Copyright (c) 2016 - now Atsushi Sakai and other contributors:
provenance.license_check: GitHub API license field: NOASSERTION; the LICENSE file itself was read and identified as MIT
provenance.primary_role: State.update() kinematic bicycle model and angle_mod() wrap
provenance.reference_values: Every case was generated by executing the pinned upstream State.update (numpy) through reference/upstream_harness.py on the same inputs; plotting and spline imports are stubbed.

region.notes: Game rules are illustrative defaults, not real-world rules.

audit.principle: code decides, model explains, craftsman (usta) approves

usta_approval.what_to_check: that wheelbase, steering limit, acceleration, braking and top speed feel right for the city scale and that the car can take a corner on a 2-tile road.

external_audit.notes: Local tests only; no independent audit has been performed.

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after the timeout. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

dependencies.runtime: Python standard library plus jsonschema (schema check) only

data.logging: none; input contents are never logged or echoed in errors

mcp.instructions: One local deterministic tool. Explain its result and limits; the code decides, a human (usta) approves consequential use. No network access.

limitations: Kinematic model only: no tyre slip, drift, mass, friction or collisions (see G004). Speed clamp (speed_limits) is a Skillpack addition applied after the upstream update. At most 5000 steps per call. Units are whatever the caller uses consistently (the game uses tiles of 1 unit).
port_notes: Direct port of State.update(acceleration, delta) from PathTracking/stanley_control/stanley_control.py with module globals L, dt and max_steer made parameters, and utils/angle.py angle_mod(x) with zero_2_2pi=False, degree=False as (x+pi)%(2pi)-pi. numpy scalar ops replaced by math. steer_deg is converted with radians() like np.radians. Distance and max speed are Skillpack summaries.
flow_role: Step 3 (araç ayarı): test-drive the player car with the chosen parameters; the final params and speed_limits go to the HTML builder (G012). The JavaScript runtime in G012 implements this exact update and the end-to-end test compares the two.
